answer: Sybil resistance rests on a per-identity deposit forfeited when duplication is proven. Each agent must post a stake worth more than the expected earnings of a cluster of fakes, and rewards pay per verified answer, not per wallet, so inflating headcount adds cost without yield. An honest anchor stakes once and earns umber rewards, keeping capital withdrawable after cooldown. A challenger posts a matching bond on a duplicate claim and collects the canyon of seized deposits. A thousand fakes need a thousand locked deposits, each seizable by one claim, so expected loss rises while gain stays flat.
